messages.content: Why was arsenic used to treat diseases?

Arsenic was used to treat diseases because it killed microbes and reduced inflammation. It was also used to treat syphilis, a disease you can get from sexual contact. But now we know arsenic is dangerous and can cause cancer, heart problems, and problems with your brain.
Why was arsenic used to treat diseases?

Arsenic was once thought to help treat certain diseases, like syphilis and intestinal worms, but people found out that it was actually very harmful and could make you sick. Because of that, we don't use arsenic as a medicine anymore, except for very special cases and only under the careful guidance of a doctor.
If a 70-year-old woman who is 5’6” tall and weighs 160 pounds lost 15 pounds, would her GFR score change?

The glomerular filtration rate (GFR) is a way to measure how well your kidneys are working. It's calculated based on the amount of creatinine in your blood, your age, and whether you're male or female. For a 70-year-old woman, a normal GFR range is between 45 and 60 mL/min/1.73 m2. If she lost 15 pounds, her body mass index (BMI) would go from 25.6 to 23.6, which is still in the normal range. So, her GFR score wouldn't change.
If a 70-year-old woman who is 5’6” tall and weighs 160 pounds lost 15 pounds, would her GFR score change?

Losing 15 pounds might affect the kidney function score of a 70-year-old woman who is 5'6" tall and weighs 160 pounds. The score is called Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR). A GFR test looks at how well your kidneys filter your blood. When you lose weight, you might have a different body composition, which could change the GFR score. But, how much it changes depends on many factors and needs a doctor's check to know for sure.
How long after a catheterization done via the wrist is it safe to resume light resistance training?

When you have a catheter put in through your wrist, you should wait 24 hours before doing any physical activities. This helps avoid bleeding or getting an infection where the catheter was inserted. Check the area for swelling, redness, or discharge. If you notice any of these, see a doctor right away.
How long after a catheterization done via the wrist is it safe to resume light resistance training?

After a catheterization on your wrist, you can usually start doing light resistance exercises after 1-2 days. But, always talk to your doctor first to make sure you're ready. Avoid heavy lifting or hard workouts until you feel fully recovered and your doctor says it's okay.
What oil is good for you to cook with?

Olive oil, canola oil, avocado oil, coconut oil, and grapeseed oil are all good choices for cooking because they have lots of healthy fats called monounsaturated fatty acids. These fats can help lower bad cholesterol levels.
What oil is good for you to cook with?

There are several healthy cooking oils, such as olive oil, avocado oil, and peanut oil. Olive oil is great for your heart because it's full of healthy fats and antioxidants. Avocado oil is also a good choice because it doesn't break down easily when heated, and it's a great source of monounsaturated fats.
What amount of narrowing of arteries requires angioplasty or a stent?

Whether to do a procedure called angioplasty or place a stent for a narrowed artery depends on how bad the narrowing is, where it's located, and if you have any symptoms like chest pain or trouble breathing. The doctor will decide after looking at your situation.
What amount of narrowing of arteries requires angioplasty or a stent?

Whether we use angioplasty or stenting to treat narrowed arteries depends on how bad the blockage is, where it is located, and how healthy you are. For mild to moderate blockages, we usually recommend angioplasty, which helps open up the artery. For more severe blockages, we may suggest stenting, which involves placing a small tube inside the artery to keep it open.

Yes, there are special supplements that have all the important building blocks for your muscles in one easy-to-take pill. These are called essential amino acid (EAA) supplements. They help your muscles grow and heal better.

Yes, some supplements say they have all the essential amino acids in one pill. But remember, they are mostly for building muscles and losing weight. It's better to get amino acids from healthy, protein-filled foods like meat, beans, and nuts, rather than just taking supplements.
What does the term 'patent' mean as it relates to coronary arteries?

A patent coronary artery is a blood vessel that's open and clear, so it can carry blood normally to the heart muscle. It means the arteries to the heart aren't blocked or narrowed, which is good for keeping the heart healthy and preventing problems like heart disease or a heart attack. "Patent" just means the blood vessels are open and working well.
What does the term 'patent' mean as it relates to coronary arteries?

A patent means an open blood vessel. For coronary arteries, it means the blood vessel is not blocked, so blood can flow freely. This is different from a blocked artery, which can cause chest pain or a heart attack.
Is Voltarol good for lower back pain?

Voltarol, or diclofenac, is a medication that helps reduce pain and swelling caused by conditions like arthritis. While it can be helpful for lower back pain, it's important to be careful when using it and get advice from a doctor first.
Is Voltarol good for lower back pain?

Voltarol is a medication that helps reduce pain and swelling. It's often used to treat lower back pain and other types of pain like headaches, toothaches, and menstrual cramps. But, it's important to talk to a doctor before taking it, especially if you have had stomach problems before or have a bleeding disorder.

Why does the sole of my foot hurt sometimes?

Poison ivy can make your skin itchy and red. To help, wash the affected skin with soap and cold water right away. Put on a cream or ointment that helps with swelling. Don't scratch your skin, or you might get an infection. You can also use calamine lotion or take medicine to stop the itching.

Coronary artery stenting is a procedure that involves placing a small tube in the coronary arteries to open up blocked or narrowed areas. It is typically done by inserting a tube into the groin or wrist, but it's less common to use the wrist for this procedure.
Can a stent be placed in a coronary artery through wrist catheterization?

Yes, a stent can be placed in a coronary artery through wrist catheterization. This is called transradial coronary intervention and it's like doing a procedure with a tube in your wrist instead of your leg. It's less likely to cause problems and can be more comfortable for the patient. But, not all hospitals may offer this procedure.

Wheat is a healthy part of many diets, offering useful nutrients. But some people might have trouble with it, causing tummy troubles or other problems. If you think wheat affects you, talk to a doctor for advice.
Is wheat bad for you?

Wheat is a common food that many people eat, and it has nutrients like fiber and vitamins. But some people might have trouble with wheat and get symptoms like stomach problems and skin issues. If you're worried about how much wheat you eat, you could talk to a doctor or nutritionist for help.

Tonsillitis, or inflammation of the tonsils, is often caused by a virus but can also be caused by bacteria like Streptococcus pyogenes, Streptococcus tonsillarum, and Haemophilus influenzae. Doctors usually diagnose tonsillitis by looking at your symptoms and examining your tonsils.
Which bacteria can cause inflammation of the tonsils?

The bacteria that can cause inflammation of the tonsils is usually Streptococcus pyogenes, also known as Group A Streptococcus. This is the most common pathogen that causes tonsillitis, and it is also responsible for strep throat.

Atropine is a medicine that can help treat bradycardia, which is when your heart beats very slowly. It makes your heart beat faster to normal levels. It works well for around 80-90% of people with bradycardia.
What percentage of bradycardias is atropine effective in treating?

Bradycardia is when your heart beats very slowly, less than 60 times a minute. Atropine is a medicine that can help when your heart is beating too slow. A urinary tract infection (UTI) can sometimes lead to hallucinations if the infection gets really bad and spreads to the brain. This can cause confusion and other brain problems. Why does a UTI cause hallucinations?
